evidence.quote: LLM-for-HLS is an open-source project focused on leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for High-Level Synthesis (HLS). This project aims to construct datasets, fine-tune LLMs, and evaluate their performance in generating HLS code based on natural language instructions. It also involves some techniques like feedback loop and chain of thoughts.
Later, we extended the orignial dataset by adding tens of new source file after thoroughly inspecting the repository https://github.com/UT-LCA/ML4Accel-Dataset/tree/main/fpga_ml_dataset/HLS_dataset.

repos.notes: First author Jiahao Gai's GitHub repo (github.com/jiahaogai, display name 'Jiahao Gai'). README describes exactly the paper's pipeline: collecting an HLS dataset (extending UT-LCA/ML4Accel-Dataset), fine-tuning CodeLlama-7b with QLoRA via axolotl, and HLS code generation with feedback loops and chain-of-thought. Repo contains train.sh/inference.sh/functionality_check.sh and data/ dirs. The paper itself has no explicit 'code available' statement, so this is own_found_by_search. Note: repo creation (Dec 2023) predates the paper publication (Jan 2025), consistent with code released during the project's development. Contains HLS (Vitis-style) C code, so it contains HLS designs.

summary: The paper's own code is jiahaogai/LLM-for-HLS (first author Jiahao Gai's repo), found by search since the paper has no explicit 'code available' statement; its README describes exactly the paper's pipeline (HLS dataset from ML4Accel, CodeLlama-7B QLoRA fine-tuning via axolotl, feedback loops + chain-of-thought), commits are by 'Jiahao Gai', and the scan confirms HLS/Vitis-style code. The paper builds its benchmark on two other repos, UCLA-DM/HLSyn and UT-LCA/ML4Accel-Dataset, both linked in the paper body (Section 3.2) and both containing HLS designs (ML4Accel verified; HLSyn holds designs in a tar.gz archive). Confidence is high for all three; no other artifacts claimed.
